      - heading "Rule (When to use Exact vs Numeric)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: • Use EXACT when the result contains surds (√), π, fractions, exponents, or symbolic parameters.
      - paragraph: • Use NUMERIC when a decimal approximation is sufficient or required for measurement.
      - paragraph: "Key idea: Exact preserves mathematical meaning; numeric introduces rounding."
      - heading "Common Misconception" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Toggling to Numeric is not “more correct”. It is an approximation. Too few digits can hide differences or make non-zero errors appear as zero.
      - complementary:
        - text: Example
        - paragraph: 1/3 ≈ 0.33333333 (8 digits)
        - paragraph: but a rounded decimal is not exactly 1/3.
